target_customer: Urology practices, hospitals and clinics that would buy a benchtop analyzer and cartridges for rapid urinary tract infection and antibiotic sensitivity testing
problem: Doctors wait days for urine culture results and often prescribe antibiotics blindly. Astek is building a point-of-care analyzer that confirms infection and indicates antibiotic sensitivity in about one hour.
business_model: Medical device: benchtop analyzer plus disposable microfluidic cartridges (not yet on the market)
product_category: Point-of-care diagnostics and rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing

founders.name: Mustafa Al-Adhami
education: University of Maryland, Baltimore County, PhD in mechanical engineering
founders.background_notes: Technical.ly (Jan 2022) says PhD in mechanical engineering from UMBC. YC page says he won business plan competitions including Baylor Business Plan as a doctoral student.

founders.name: Kevin Tran
founders.background_notes: Named as cofounder and CTO by Technical.ly (Jan 2022); not on the YC page. Background not found.

competitors.name: Astrego Diagnostics (PA-100 AST)
competitors.what: Rapid urine antibiotic susceptibility test system for urinary tract infections
competitors.traction_then: Not stated; product launched in Europe in 2023
competitors.funding_then: Sysmex agreed Dec 2019 to take a 24.99% stake; later full acquisition May 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: Microfluidic cartridges that isolate bacteria and measure oxygen consumption or optical changes, requiring a medical device, clinical validation and FDA clearance; research-grade hardware plus regulatory path.

defensibility.rationale: Patents, university IP and an FDA pathway raise barriers, though other rapid AST developers are well funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors advanced on their own timelines (Sysmex Astrego launched PA-100 in Europe in 2023 and won the Longitude Prize in 2024); no source of any copying or acquisition of Astek.

market_need_then: Antimicrobial resistance and slow urine culture turnaround were widely recognized problems; the Longitude Prize on AMR rewarded rapid tests. Founder motivation came from his grandfather's UTI treatment delay (company site).

branding.name_origin: Astek is not explained in sources opened; the product name Jiddu is said by a search summary to be named after what the founder called his grandfather as a child (360Dx snippet, not opened). Earlier platform name Eugris.

identity.voice_and_tone: Urgent, mission driven and patient focused: 'Saving lives through antibiotic sensitivity precision diagnostics' (company site)

branding.brand_signature: Product named after the founder's grandfather (unverified)

brand_strength.rationale: Known mainly in the Maryland startup ecosystem and trade press; no brand press found and the product is pre-launch.

pivots.from: Eugris platform for sepsis antibiotic guidance via oxygen consumption
pivots.to: JIDDU analyzer focused on urinary tract infections first
pivots.why: Not stated; wedge narrowed to urine with other sample types in development

outcome_analysis: Astek is active and pre-revenue. After YC S21 it closed about $850K in early 2022, later added seed and pre-Series A money from Maryland funds and angels, and the YC page claims over $5M raised in total. The company targeted market entry in 2025 pending FDA clearance, which is not confirmed. Hardware and regulatory timelines are the main risks.
notes: YC page states over 5M raised; MTEC profile cites 5.3M; CB Insights 3.73M; VCBacked 500K (latest only); these are unverified totals. The Jan 2022 round of 850K is from Technical.ly with no investors named. Pre-Series A (Mar 2024) lead She's Independent, amount undisclosed; other named backers include TEDCO, Maryland Momentum Fund, Wexford, AYANA, Harvard Management Seed Capital, Goldin Ventures. USM seed announcement (June 2023) and CityBiz could not be opened (503, 403) and 360Dx/GenomeWeb returned 403; not worked around. 360Dx raise target (15M vs 25M) is from a search summary only. Competitor list limited to one batch-near source; Accelerate and bioMerieux are blood culture focused.
